reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) does not address any of the key premises. E1 discusses magnetocaloric properties of bulk HEAs and mentions thermal conductivity as a pragmatic engineering factor, but provides no data on thin films, substrate effects, or thermal lag. E2 describes general PVD deposition of intermetallic films and notes higher thermal conductivity of thin films compared to bulk, but does not link substrate conductivity to magnetic hysteresis or magnetocaloric response. The premises rely entirely on uncited general principles.
premises: Substrate thermal conductivity governs local temperature evolution in the film during magnetic cycles.
Enhanced heat dissipation reduces thermal lag, lowering the effective energy barrier for domain reversal.
Reduced thermal lag leads to sharper magnetocaloric transition and reduced hysteresis.
The effect is more pronounced at higher cycling frequencies where heat-transfer limits are critical.
Substrate-induced strain effects can be controlled or decoupled from thermal effects.
